chunks: Ahmad ibn Abi Abdillah narrated from his father, from Wahb, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:
The Commander of the Faithful (peace be upon him) said: 'The sale of 'Arbun (earnest money/deposit) is not valid unless it is paid in cash from the price.'

key_terms.الْعَرَبُونِ: Earnest money or deposit paid in advance in a sales contract

ai.seo_question: What is the condition for the validity of 'Arbun (earnest money) in Islamic sales contracts?
ai.summary: Reported by Imam al-Sadiq (AS) from Imam Ali (AS), this hadith clarifies the validity of 'Arbun (earnest money) in sales contracts, stipulating that the deposit must be paid in immediate cash (thaman) to ensure clarity and avoid ambiguity (gharar). This ruling reflects the Shia juristic emphasis on precise monetary exchange in commercial transactions, distinguishing it from credit-based arrangements which may introduce uncertainty. The requirement for cash payment underscores the importance of tangible, immediate value transfer in Islamic contract law.
